label: Person
name: Adam Patachich
summary:
Adam Patachich (1716–1784) was a Hungarian Catholic bishop and archbishop who served successively as Bishop of Oradea (Nagyvárad) and Archbishop of Kalocsa-Bács, becoming one of the most cultured and enlightened ecclesiastical patrons of eighteenth-century Hungary. Born into Hungarian nobility, he pursued an ecclesiastical career that combined episcopal administration with enthusiastic patronage of the arts, music, and literature.

As Archbishop of Kalocsa (1776–1784), Patachich transformed the archiepiscopal seat into a centre of cultural life, establishing one of Hungary's most significant Baroque libraries—the Patachich Library—and hosting musicians, poets, and scholars. He was a gifted composer himself and promoted the performance of orchestral music at the archiepiscopal court, making Kalocsa briefly competitive with the great musical centres of Vienna and Esztergom. His library, now part of the Kalocsa Archiepiscopal Library, remains one of the finest collections of Baroque manuscripts and printed books in Hungary.

Patachich's career reflects the Enlightenment-era Catholic archbishop as cultural entrepreneur—a bishop who saw the patronage of learning and arts as integral to the Church's civilising mission. His legacy endures in the Kalocsa Library, which he bequeathed to the archdiocese and which continues to preserve his extraordinary collection, making him one of the most significant cultural benefactors in Hungarian Catholic history.
